headword: {侵食作用|しんしょくさよう}

definitions.explanation: The geological process by which water, wind, or ice gradually wears away rock and soil and carries the material elsewhere.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}の{侵食作用|しんしょくさよう}で{谷|たに}ができる。
{風|かぜ}の{侵食作用|しんしょくさよう}が{岩|いわ}を{削|けず}る。
examples.english: Wind erosion wears away the rock.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{年月|ねんげつ}をかけた{侵食作用|しんしょくさよう}が{地形|ちけい}を{変|か}えていく。
examples.english: Erosion over long ages gradually reshapes the landscape.

notes:
USAGE: {侵食作用|しんしょくさよう} is the geological action of erosion, combining {侵食|しんしょく} (erosion) with {作用|さよう} (action, effect). It is common in earth-science contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水|みず}の{侵食作用|しんしょくさよう}: water erosion
- {侵食作用|しんしょくさよう}を{受|う}ける: to undergo erosion

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {風化作用|ふうかさよう}: weathering — the breakdown of rock in place, without transport
- {堆積|たいせき}: deposition — the opposite process, in which sediment builds up
